newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate 11.5 pct in lively trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate 11.5 pct in lively trade.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 11.5 percent from 11 percent on Tuesday, as high demand for fresh kuna funds livened trade after the festive lull, dealers said.
"Companies began paying their debts and the banks resumed extending loans, which created a good demand," a dealer said.
Tuesday's trade totalled 117.7 million kuna, of which some 69 million kuna was new borrowing. But demand from borrowers for a further 17.3 million kuna could not be met.
Insurers rolled over previous 24 million kuna loans at nine and 15 percent rates.
Most of the rates remained relatively stable. "Creditors decided they could not achieve a higher price for their money on a substantial offer," the dealer said.
Term loans were struck at rates varying from 11 percent for one week loans to 15 percent for one month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday at 5.5573 against the dollar and 3.5612 against the mark. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
